subject.gist: Rob adds fish to tackle greenhouse mosquitoes, discovers aquaponics, and automates his growing system while still wrestling with sticky vents and pests.

story.text: Rob starts with a greenhouse for garden seedlings, then adds a water tank to steady its temperature. Mosquitoes lead him to add fish, and keeping their water clean leads him to aquaponics. He rebuilds the greenhouse around fish tanks and planted beds, delighted by how well things grow. Calling himself a lazy gardener, he automates feeding and ventilation, though the vents still need a helping hand. Inside the house, he shows a smaller system made with storage containers. He still pulls weeds and squashes aphids, and enjoys taking cucumbers to work even when colleagues question the fish-waste fertilizer.

features.title: Recirculating fish and plant water system
features.description: Water circulates from the fish tank through planted grow beds, drains into a lower sump and is pumped back to the fish. Rob explains that bacteria convert ammonia excreted by the fish into nitrites and then nitrates, which the plants take up as fertilizer, cleaning the circulating water. He describes fish food and the resulting fish waste as the inputs that feed the plants.
features.unknown: The camera does not trace every concealed pipe or establish water chemistry, replacement-water demand or microbiological safety.
